subject: Biology
title: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
summary: Mendel (1856–1863, garden pea) proposed the laws of inheritance: dominance, segregation and independent assortment. Monohybrid F₂ ratio 3:1 (phenotype), 1:2:1 (genotype); dihybrid F₂ 9:3:3:1.
Deviations from Mendel: incomplete dominance (snapdragon 1:2:1), co-dominance (ABO blood groups), multiple alleles, pleiotropy and polygenic inheritance (skin colour).

The chromosomal theory of inheritance (Sutton and Boveri) placed genes on chromosomes; Morgan's Drosophila work showed linkage and recombination. Sex is determined by chromosomes (XX–XY, XX–XO, ZW–ZZ) or haplodiploidy.

Mutations and chromosomal changes cause disorders: Mendelian (haemophilia, colour blindness, sickle-cell anaemia, phenylketonuria, thalassemia) and chromosomal (Down's, Klinefelter's, Turner's syndromes). Pedigree analysis traces traits in families.

formulas.name: Monohybrid cross
formulas.formula: TT × tt → F₁ Tt (all tall);  F₁ selfed → F₂ phenotype 3:1, genotype 1:2:1 (TT : Tt : tt)

formulas.name: Test cross
formulas.formula: F₁ (Tt) × recessive parent (tt) → 1:1 (monohybrid);  dihybrid test cross → 1:1:1:1
formulas.when: Finding the unknown genotype of a dominant phenotype.

formulas.name: Dihybrid cross
formulas.formula: RRYY × rryy → F₁ RrYy;  F₂ phenotype 9:3:3:1;  9 genotypes;  4 gamete types from F₁
formulas.when: Two characters — law of independent assortment.

formulas.name: General counts
formulas.formula: gametes = 2ⁿ;  F₂ genotypes = 3ⁿ;  F₂ phenotypes (complete dominance) = 2ⁿ  (n = heterozygous gene pairs)

formulas.name: Incomplete dominance
formulas.formula: snapdragon (Antirrhinum): RR red × rr white → Rr pink;  F₂ phenotype = genotype = 1:2:1

formulas.name: Co-dominance and multiple alleles
formulas.formula: ABO: alleles Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i;  Iᴬ and Iᴮ co-dominant, both dominant over i;  6 genotypes, 4 phenotypes (A, B, AB, O)

formulas.name: Pleiotropy and polygenic traits
formulas.formula: pleiotropy: one gene, many effects (phenylketonuria);  polygenic: several genes add up (human skin colour, height)

formulas.name: Linkage and recombination
formulas.formula: genes close together on a chromosome are inherited together (linkage);  recombination frequency ∝ distance (Sturtevant used it to map genes);  Morgan: white-eye/yellow-body ~1.3% recombination, white-eye/miniature wing ~37.2%

formulas.name: Sex determination types
formulas.formula: XX–XY: humans, Drosophila (male heterogametic);  XX–XO: grasshopper;  ZW–ZZ: birds (female heterogametic);  haplodiploid: honey bee (males from unfertilised eggs, n = 16; females 2n = 32)

formulas.name: X-linked recessive
formulas.formula: haemophilia, colour blindness;  carrier mother (XᴴXʰ) × normal father → 50% sons affected, 50% daughters carriers
formulas.note: Affected females are rare — they need two copies of the recessive allele.

formulas.name: Autosomal recessive disorders
formulas.formula: sickle-cell anaemia (GAG → GUG, glutamic acid → valine at 6th position of β-globin);  phenylketonuria (no phenylalanine hydroxylase);  thalassemia (α: chromosome 16, β: chromosome 11 — reduced globin synthesis)
formulas.mistake: Thalassemia is a quantitative problem (too little globin); sickle-cell is qualitative (wrong globin).

formulas.name: Chromosomal disorders
formulas.formula: Down's syndrome: trisomy 21 (47);  Klinefelter's: 47, XXY (male, gynaecomastia, sterile);  Turner's: 45, X0 (female, sterile, rudimentary ovaries)

formulas.name: Pedigree symbols
formulas.formula: square = male, circle = female, shaded = affected, double line = consanguineous mating

examples.title: Dihybrid fraction
examples.problem: In a dihybrid F₂, what fraction shows both dominant traits?

examples.title: Gametes from AaBbCc
examples.problem: How many types of gametes does AaBbCc form?

examples.title: Genotypes in dihybrid F₂
examples.problem: How many genotypes appear in a dihybrid F₂?

examples.title: Colour-blind son
examples.problem: A carrier woman marries a normal man. Chance that a son is colour blind?
examples.solution: Sons get X from mother: half get Xᶜ → 50% of sons.

examples.title: Blood group of children
examples.problem: Parents are Iᴬi and Iᴮi. Possible blood groups of children?
examples.solution: IᴬIᴮ (AB), Iᴬi (A), Iᴮi (B) and ii (O) — all four, each with probability 1/4.

examples.title: Why Drosophila?
examples.solution: Grows on simple synthetic medium, completes its life cycle in about two weeks, a single mating gives many offspring, males and females are easy to tell apart, and it has many hereditary variations visible under low-power microscopes.

topics.title: Mendel's experimental design
topics.explain: Mendel used 14 true-breeding pea varieties with seven pairs of contrasting traits; pea is self-pollinating, short-lived and easy to cross. He used large samples and statistics. His work was rediscovered in 1900 by de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak.

topics.title: Law of dominance and segregation
topics.explain: Characters are controlled by discrete factors (genes) occurring in pairs; in a dissimilar pair one dominates (dominance). Alleles separate during gamete formation so each gamete gets only one (segregation) — the law of purity of gametes.

topics.title: Punnett square
topics.explain: A graphical grid developed by Reginald C. Punnett to calculate the probability of all possible genotypes of offspring in a genetic cross.

topics.title: Mutation
topics.explain: A change in DNA sequence that alters genotype and phenotype. Point mutation: change in a single base pair (sickle-cell anaemia). Frameshift mutations: insertion or deletion of bases. Mutagens include UV radiation and chemicals.

topics.title: Chromosomal theory of inheritance
topics.explain: Sutton and Boveri noted that chromosomes, like Mendel's factors, occur in pairs, segregate at gamete formation and assort independently. Sutton united chromosomal segregation with Mendelian principles.

topics.title: Aneuploidy and polyploidy
topics.explain: Failure of chromatid segregation in cell division gives gain or loss of a chromosome (aneuploidy). Failure of cytokinesis after telophase gives a whole extra set (polyploidy), common in plants.

ratta: Snapdragon 1:2:1 = incomplete dominance;  ABO = co-dominance + multiple alleles.
Grasshopper XO;  birds ZW female;  honey bee haplodiploid.
Down 21 trisomy;  Klinefelter XXY;  Turner XO.
